chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥajjāl, from Thaʿlabah ibn Maymūn, from Zurārah, that he said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about the grave: how many may enter it? He said: “That is up to the guardian; if he wishes, he may make an odd number enter, and if he wishes, he may make an even number enter.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: Then the deceased is drawn into his grave from the direction of his feet so that his head reaches it first, just as he came first into the world in his emergence to it from his mother’s womb. And he should say, upon beholding the grave, the supplication (1), and when he takes hold of him he says: “In the name of Allah, and by Allah, and in the way of Allah,” completing the supplication (2).

Then he places him on his right side and turns him toward the qiblah, unties the knots of his shroud from his head until his face appears, places his cheek upon the earth, and also unties the knots of his shroud from the direction of his feet. Then he places the bricks over him and says, while placing them, the supplication (3).

key_terms.الدُّعَاءَ: the supplication recited during the burial procedure
key_terms.الْقَبْرِ: the grave into which the deceased is placed
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the direction toward which the deceased is turned in burial
key_terms.الْوَلِيِّ: the guardian or responsible relative who decides the burial arrangement
key_terms.شَفْعًا: an even number of people entering the grave
key_terms.كَفَنِهِ: the shroud wrapped around the deceased
key_terms.وَتْرًا: an odd number of people entering the grave

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about how the deceased should be placed in the grave and how many people may enter it?
ai.summary: This report discusses rulings and etiquette related to placing the deceased into the grave, including who may enter the grave and how the body should be positioned. It also mentions prescribed supplications at different moments of burial, reflecting the ritual care and reverence observed in funerary practice.
